solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: With excitement in abundance, for the most part

indicators.note: most of the word, so the final letter is dropped from the synonym for 'in abundance'

parts.note: a-gogo is an informal phrase meaning plentifully, in abundance

explanation.surface: Someone describing a thrill that comes in large amounts, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims the last O from AGOGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagerly expectant and excited, as in waiting all agog for news, is the adjective's usual sense.

clue.text: Revamped bar's got up as this?

definitions.text: Revamped bar's got up as this?

indicators.note: something revamped is remade and reorganised, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's here supplies an S along with the word bar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub that has been refurbished and dressed up might end up as one of these upmarket places.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a bar that has been revamped and smartened up is just what this kind of place is.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub given a smart makeover with restaurant-quality food is the classic example of the trend described.

clue.text: Film broadcast when I wed tonight

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so the following words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A newlywed telling someone when the TV station will show the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1939 Civil War epic starring Vivien Leigh and Clark Gable is one of the best-known movies ever made.

clue.text: It'll earn a little money to get drinks

definitions.text: It'll earn a little money to get drinks

parts.words: It'll earn a little money to get drinks
parts.note: a teenager's newspaper delivery job brings in pocket money; read differently, paper money (banknotes) buys a round of drinks

explanation.surface: Someone describing a small job whose wages go on a few beers.
explanation.walkthrough: PAPER is slang for banknotes and ROUND is a set of drinks bought for a group, so the clue also describes a round paid for with notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivering newspapers door to door is the traditional small-earning job for British teenagers.

clue.text: 21 structure poor, built shoddily

indicators.note: done shoddily means put together badly, so these letters are assembled in a jumbled way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic complaining that a building is poorly and cheaply constructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 refers to the answer at 21-across, SOVIET.
explanation.definitionFit: The policy-making committee of the Communist Party was the chief governing body of the Soviet system.

clue.text: Lover of country dance style reeling at wild party…

indicators.note: reeling means spinning round, so the dance style's name turns back to front

parts.note: tap is a style of dance done in metal-tipped shoes
a riot can mean a raucous, uproarious party

explanation.surface: A folk dancer spinning wildly at a rowdy party, apparently a lover of country dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover of country dance' wants to be one phrase; the definition stops at 'country'. 'reeling' turns TAP into PAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loves and loyally supports their nation is exactly what the word describes.

clue.text: … to have another dance, perhaps making new arrangement

parts.note: the prefix re- means again, giving another go at something
a jig is a lively folk dance

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: the party-goer wants to dance again, perhaps in a new formation.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun this means a reorganisation or reshuffle, a fresh arrangement of something.

clue.text: Under the influence of drugs, I take solvent, remove top and expose myself occasionally

parts.note: on means taking a drug, as in 'he's on heroin'
C is cocaine and E is ecstasy in slang
to nab is to grab or take

indicators.note: taking the top off a down entry drops its first letter

parts.note: glue is a solvent abused by sniffing
to moon is to bare one's buttocks

explanation.surface: A wild confession of drug-taking, glue-sniffing and stripping off, with the comic claim that it only happens now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove top' takes the G off GLUE, a solvent sniffed for a high.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very rarely, a rare event likened to a second full moon in one month.

clue.text: Beak's not available — transaction's unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a sale is a transaction; the 's is part of the surface only

explanation.surface: A magistrate's not around, so a deal goes uncompleted.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak is slang for nose (and for a magistrate); 'unfinished' cuts SALE to SAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the nose, which slang calls a beak.

clue.text: Underwear that might make object out of butt?

definitions.text: that might make object out of butt?
definitions.meaning: giving 'butt' only one T leaves 'but', which as a verb means to object

explanation.surface: A garment that might somehow turn a backside into a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' is the verb (to raise a 'but'), not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless vest worn under a shirt or by athletes is a kind of undergarment.

clue.text: Merry horseman missing vital round at point-to-point?

indicators.note: missing says one word is left out of another

parts.note: a jockey is a professional rider
key means vital or essential
O is round in shape
S and E are two compass points

explanation.surface: A rider at a point-to-point (an amateur steeplechase) who has missed a crucial lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing vital' takes KEY out of JOCKEY to leave JOC.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective means playful and humorous, close to cheerful or jolly.

clue.text: Comes up against Hertfordshire non-league side, I gather

definitions.note: the clue speaks as the object itself: a cord that gathers fabric

parts.note: a team draws another when paired with them in a cup draw
Tring Athletic is a non-league football club from Tring in Hertfordshire

explanation.surface: A sports fan hearing that their team has been paired with a minor Hertfordshire football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gather' looks like 'I understand'; it is the answer speaking. Hertfordshire is an English county north of London; non-league means outside the professional leagues.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord threaded through a hem is pulled to gather the fabric, as at a bag's neck.

clue.text: Head off demands for money, they're troublesome

indicators.note: taking off the head removes the first letter

parts.note: bills are requests for payment

explanation.surface: Advice to stop invoices before they arrive, since they cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like 'prevent'; it drops the B of BILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubles, misfortunes and ailments go by this plural noun.

clue.text: Treated as past it, offer nark sexual favours

definitions.meaning: retired from work because considered too old
to put out is slang for agreeing to sex, and a grass is a police informer or nark

explanation.surface: An ageing person sidelined, and a lurid suggestion of bribing an informer with sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Nark is British slang for a police informer, as is grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from retiring an old horse to pasture, so treating someone as too old to work.

clue.text: It's a faux pas to say die, darling

indicators.note: to say means the words are heard spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: go is a euphemism for die, and cherie is French for darling

explanation.surface: Someone saying it is tactless to tell your loved one to drop dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactless or socially awkward act is a blunder, the same idea as a social gaffe.

clue.text: Non-English Streep character's attempt at tortured reasoning

indicators.note: E is the abbreviation for English, so it is taken out

parts.note: Meryl Streep played Sophie in the film Sophie's Choice
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A film critic finding a foreign-accented Meryl Streep role's effort unconvincing.
explanation.walkthrough: Sophie is Polish, so 'Non-English' fits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever but fallacious argument, twisting logic to persuade, is what the term means.

clue.text: Shut up — that's what you get when you kiss ass!

definitions.text: that's what you get when you kiss ass!
definitions.meaning: kissing a backside would leave a ...

explanation.surface: A rebuke to a toady: stop talking, and look where flattery gets you.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BUTT ON YOUR LIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an instruction to keep quiet, a rude command for silence.

clue.text: Indeed, right before origins of dawn of time?

definitions.text: Indeed, right before origins of dawn of time?

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes or indeed

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so the opening letter of each of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: A question about what came right before the beginning of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the very origin of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for a very long time ago, the beginning of time itself.

clue.text: Journey endlessly east in plane, say?

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter

parts.note: a trek is a long journey

explanation.surface: A long eastbound journey by aircraft that seems never to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the plane tree, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The London plane is a common deciduous species, so a plane is an example of the woody plant.

clue.text: Cried off punch containing fruit juice and wine

indicators.note: containing means one piece holds another inside it
off means taken away, so one word comes out of the other

parts.note: sangria is a punch of red wine and fruit
sang means cried out in song
OJ is shorthand for orange juice

explanation.surface: Someone who declined a fruity punch and had a glass of red instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cried off' looks like 'withdrew'; it takes SANG off SANGRIA, leaving RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This red wine comes from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Not keen on training, I eat lunch in mess, taking time

indicators.note: taking means holding something inside
in a mess means jumbled up

explanation.surface: A lazy recruit eating lunch in the mess hall rather than exercising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like an army canteen; 'in mess' jumbles I EAT LUNCH, and 'taking' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone averse to exercise or sport lacks physical fitness and athletic ability.

clue.text: Extreme left and right dominating parliament in the end in Ukraine

indicators.note: in places the whole group inside the country code

parts.note: UA is the international code for Ukraine

indicators.note: dominating here means standing either side of and hemming in
in the end means the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A news report on left and right extremists controlling Ukraine's parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dominating' puts L and R around T, the end of 'parliament'; 'in' puts all that inside UA.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adjective this means beyond the usual, radical or excessive.

clue.text: Cold war rival's provided what was missing in Nam?

parts.note: so means provided that, as in 'so long as'

indicators.note: asks what part has gone from the short name, so the full name loses the short form's letters

parts.note: Nam is American slang for the country Vietnam, a clipped form of its full name

explanation.surface: A question about the Cold War: did a rival power supply what the Vietnam war lacked?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nam' is American slang for Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: The USSR was America's chief opponent through the Cold War standoff.

clue.text: Suddenly appear old-fashioned, reactionary and unfashionable

indicators.note: reactionary suggests going back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: trad is short for traditional
out means out of fashion

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly revealed as outdated, reactionary and passé.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reactionary' turns TRAD into DART.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge with a quick sudden movement, as a mouse from a hole.

clue.text: Polish company backed extension to building, one that goes with the flow?

definitions.text: one that goes with the flow?

parts.note: to sand is to smooth or polish
a cast is a company of actors

indicators.note: backed means turned round to run back to front

parts.note: an el is a wing or extension of a building, per Chambers

explanation.surface: A Polish firm reversing an extension, alongside someone who goes with the flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is the verb, not the nationality. 'backed' turns EL into LE. The definition jokes that the incoming tide washes it away.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach sculpture of damp sand is carried off when the tide flows in.

clue.text: Votes against courses turning to the left initially?

indicators.note: the first letter is a compass point that turns to another

parts.note: ways are routes or courses

explanation.surface: Ballots opposing a change of direction to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Morph intended W (west) to turn to N (north), but that is a right turn, as the setter admitted on the blog.
explanation.definitionFit: In a parliamentary division, no votes are counted against the motion.
